svg.title: Product Operating Model
svg.desc: A3 landscape reference poster for moving to a product operating model: six shifts (projects to products, output to outcomes, feature teams to empowered teams, requirements to discovery, dated roadmaps to strategy and bets, order-taking to partnership), each with tools and a 1–5 self-assessment, what changes when AI makes building cheaper, and signs the change is only a rename.
svg.text: Organise around long-lived products and the outcomes they create, not temporary projects and the features they ship.
Lead the Organisation · Inspired by Transformed (Marty Cagan, SVPG) and Project to Product (Mik Kersten)
Fund and staff long-lived products, not temporary projects whose teams break up at
Judge success by changes in customer and business results, not by features shipped
Give teams problems to solve, not features to build, and trust them to decide how.
Test whether an idea is valuable, usable, feasible and viable before building it,
Focus on the few problems that matter most, and say what you'll learn as well as
Product teams work with the rest of the business as partners, not as a service that
When code is cheap, building the wrong thing becomes the expensive mistake.
Prototypes take hours, so run more experiments, each with a clear stop rule.
Smaller teams can look after more, so watch for overload and slipping quality.
Name who is accountable for what AI decides and produces, at every stage.
Tools in this kit: AI in Delivery · AI Working Agreement · 1% Experiment Canvas
Project managers retitled product managers, doing the same job
Teams still handed lists of features with dates
Funding still approved project by project
Success still measured by on time and on budget
No time for discovery: every idea goes straight to build
Each tick points back to a shift above. Start with the one that hurts most.
“Which shift would make the biggest difference here, and what's stopping it?”
“What would we stop doing if teams owned outcomes?”
Lead the Organisation · Outcomes Over Output · Evidence, Not Opinion
